He was right. item.title: NFL insider provides major update to Jonathan Taylor trade talk
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) reacts after rushing for a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the first half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images As the NFL trade deadline nears, the Indianapolis Colts still haven’t decided the fate of superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, but the lines have been open. Although a trade isn’t guaranteed, the opportunity makes sense, as the organization is aiming for a rebuild, and an RB with Taylor’s skill set could bring back some essential pieces for the roster. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the teams that have expressed interest in trading for Taylor include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants, sources said. Recently, ESPN’s Stephen Holder reported that the Colts were offered a package that included a second-round pick and a later-round pick for Taylor, according to a source . But Holder noted that Taylor is “the team’s best remaining asset,” and the Colts reportedly want a deal that mirrors the one that sent RB Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers. The Carolina Panthers traded McCaffrey to the 49ers in 2022 for a pick each in the second, third, fourth, and fifth rounds, which played out to be more than a steal. Thursday morning, Rapoport took to NFL Network’s Good Morning Football to provide an update on the “Taylor sweepstakes.” “Where we are at is essentially where we have been,” Rapoport said . “Which is several teams interested in Taylor, willing to offer a significant pick package, but maybe not quite what Ed Dodds, who is running personnel now in place of Chris Ballard, who was fired, wants and what the organization wants; they want a Christian McCaffrey-type package for Jonathan Taylor. “It’s clear they don’t have it; otherwise, they would have obviously made the trade. The other part of this thing is that this is someone they don’t really want to trade. This is someone they believe is a big part of their future; they’d like to build around him, so it would take a big package to get the Colts to move on from him.” Taylor is the second-leading rusher in Colts history with 8,208 yards, trailing only Hall of Famer Edgerrin James (9,226), and he leads the franchise with 77 rushing touchdowns. This season, he has already rushed for 610 yards and leads the team with eight touchdowns. While the Colts look to remain firm on any Taylor trade conversations, Rapoport also mentioned the possibility of WR Josh Downs, who requested a trade, being shipped off, as several teams need a receiver and the price would be significantly lower. item.description: During my tenure at Pinstripe Alley—hell, during my entire time as a baseball fan—I’ve never been shy about delving into the team’s history and exploring the lives of its long roll call of players, both incredible and regrettable. We provide plenty of other coverage on the current-day activities of the teams, so I like having one spot per day on the schedule to open the ol’ books and tell a story. Whether it’s remembering championship teams , Top 100 players , or notable free agent signings , there’s always something out there to explore. For the past three years , we’ve celebrated the 25th anniversary of the 1998-2000 Yankees dynasty by doing a diary on all their regular season and playoff activity. The final pages were written this past October, so it’s time for a new daily project. With that in mind, we’ll ring in the new year by beginning the Yankees Birthdays series. Every day in 2026, we’ll have a new Yankees figure to discuss whose birthday happened to fall on that day. Some days will feature far more famous stars than others! But that just adds to the challenge and our interest in the exercise. Happy new year and happy 365 days of Yankees birthdays! item.description: The Seattle Seahawks’ 2010 acquisition of Marshawn Lynch became one of the most influential in-season trades in franchise history. The move brought him from the Buffalo Bills and helped establish the physical offensive identity that eventually carried Seattle to a Super Bowl championship. The trade became official Oct. 5, 2010, after Seattle sent Buffalo a 2011 fourth-round draft pick and a conditional 2012 selection that ultimately became a fifth-rounder. Lynch was seeking a fresh opportunity after losing his starting role with the Bills, and Seahawks coach Pete Carroll strongly pushed for the deal. Carroll believed the running back’s physical style and personality could help change the direction of the franchise. He continued developing into one of the NFL’s most productive running backs over the following seasons. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: DeMarcus Lawrence has no worries about Seahawks defense, but silence on dismal offense is loud
item.description: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images DeMarcus Lawrence has no worries about Seahawks defense, but silence on dismal offense is loud appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Seattle Seahawks coming off the disappointing loss to the Chicago Bears, 34-17, the defense has been focused by many as being the underwhelming unit from the contest. As the Seahawks especially failed in the red zone against the Bears, defensive star DeMarcus Lawrence would speak on the outlook of the unit ahead of Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. Speaking to the media on Thursday, Lawrence was asked about the defense with the team now at a 4-4 record, coming right after winning the Super Bowl last season. Lawrence expressed that the defense is “right where we need to be in all honesty,” according to Greg Bell. “I feel like us as a defense, we right where we need to be in all honesty,” Lawrence said. “It’s just really the game of football, and what I see, I think us as a team, Coach McDonald, see it all the same, and it’s just one play at a time, complementary football, and that’s our style. So it’s kind of hard to just sit up here and just focus on one unit when we are a collective.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While Seattle has been a great defensive unit as a whole, the team ranks last in the league in red zone efficiency , per Brady Henderson of ESPN, culminating in allowing the Bears to score all four times their offense was inside the 20-yard line. “The Seahawks’ defense is allowing the fifth-fewest points in the NFL, but they’re last in red zone efficiency after allowing the Bears to score touchdowns on all four of their trips inside the 20. When asked about that issue today, DeMarcus Lawrence put it on his shoulders,” Henderson wrote on X, formerly Twitter. At any rate, Lawrence and the Seahawks look to improve Sunday against the Cardinals. item.title: Terry Bradshaw reacts to Joe Buck and Troy Aikman feud
item.description: Jan 19, 2020; Santa Clara, CA USA; Terry Bradshaw before the NFC Championship Game between the San Francisco 49ers and Green Bay Packers at Levin's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcasts with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have looked as normal as always, but behind the scenes, the duo has continued to feud. Issues between the two reportedly stem from Buck agreeing to a six-year extension worth more than $100 million in September that would keep him as ESPN’s voice for Monday Night Football . Aikman, on the other hand, whose contract is set to expire after this season, has yet to agree to a deal and may be in jeopardy of being replaced. Ahead of ESPN’s MNF broadcast of the Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game, the longtime partners got into an argument in the booth, according to Front Office Sports . That argument “nearly got physical off air,” a source told In Touch . Despite the tension, both have remained professional on air, but many spectators and fellow commentators are itching to know the real story. Recently, Fox NFL Sunday analyst and co-host Terry Bradshaw joined The Brian Kilmeade Show to give some clarity on the topic. “I have talked to Buck via text and told him I don’t assume everything I’m reading is correct, and I’ve known Troy Aikman for a while; they’re both real good friends of mine,” Bradshaw said . “I don’t understand. Troy has the big contract now, and Joe Buck got a big contract. I don’t want to believe that it’s the money that Buck got that’s got Troy upset, because Troy is making big money. “I have heard, I’ve heard that they were going to go into ESPN together and get a new deal together. Joe evidently got his before Troy, and that seems to be the rift; it’s about money. And I find that hard to believe because Troy Aikman is not like that; he’s not like that. My understanding right now is things are okay.” With almost half of the NFL season already over, it will be interesting to see if Buck and Aikman can remain composed until their Super Bowl broadcast, which may be their last together. item.title: Gronkowski’s Spike Story Proves Fans Built The Legend
item.description: Patriots head coach Bill Belichick talks with tight end Rob Gronkowski in the first half as the New England Patriots host the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium. Rob Gronkowski admits the fans created his most famous celebration, not him. Just before his Saturday induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame, this truth strikes with great force. The tight end spent 30 minutes on Thursday talking to reporters about the moment that changed NFL culture forever. He did not invent the spike to look cool. He did it because the crowd went wild and he could not stop. The Real Story Behind The Spike Gronkowski explained that he never planned for the move to become a symbol. He just wanted to celebrate a touchdown in a way high school and college rules banned. When he finally got to the NFL, he spiked the ball. The fans went berserk. The reaction was so loud that he kept doing it. “There’s one thing that I would say that truly stands out, and I would just say the Gronk Spike,” Gronkowski said, via video conference call, according to the Boston Herald . He called the move lethal and legendary. The celebration summed up his career because it meant a touchdown. It was a rave on the field. He kept doing it because the fans demanded it. You cannot have the spike without the people screaming for it. A Missing Owner And A Big Weekend Not everyone will be there to cheer him on. Patriots owner Robert Kraft will miss the ceremony due to back surgery. Doctors told him to stay off his feet, so he cannot travel. All six Super Bowl victories occurred while Kraft was in charge. His absence is felt deeply. Yet the celebration goes on. Patriot Place Plaza will host the induction at 1 p.m. on Saturday. Tom Brady will also be in Foxboro to broadcast his first Patriots game with FOX Sports. He will watch from the booth while the team honors the tight end. The 2016 Super Bowl LI-winning team gets a special 10th-anniversary honor during Sunday’s game against the Packers. It shows how deep the roots go. Gronkowski joked about how much fun he expects to have this weekend. At age 22, he said the experience would have been a perfect 10. Now he expects an 8.7. This figure directly references the No. 87 jersey he donned with the Patriots. “It means everything about my NFL career with the Patriots, ust to be able to be recognized with just the greats that were all before me,” Gronkowski said. He is joining a short list of legends. Julian Edelman was inducted in 2025, Tom Brady in 2024, and Mike Vrabel in 2023. Kraft is still waiting for his own turn in Canton. The tight end knows he is part of something bigger than himself. The Hall of Fame is the final chapter.

item.title: Roberto Mancini Calls up Only One Lazio Player for Italy Camp
item.description: Roberto Mancini Calls up Only One Lazio Player for Italy Camp Italy head coach Roberto Mancini called up 31 players for the November international break, including Lazio midfielder Davide Frattesi. Davide Frattesi Keeps His Place in Italy Squad The 61-year-old, who recently returned to the Azzurri dugout, had already called up the former Sassuolo player for the extended September-October international break. The Roman was heavily involved in the action, with many considering him among Italy’s best overall performers. Therefore, Mancini’s decision to recall the 27-year-old was hardly a surprise, even if his form slightly dipped after a sensational start to his Lazio stint. Zaccagni Injured, Floriani Mussolini Overlooked Frattesi won’t be joined by any of his Lazio teammates. His club captain, Mattia Zaccagni, was in fine form, but he suffered a muscle injury during Sunday’s win over Cagliari, which could keep him out for a month. Romano Floriani Mussolini was said to be on Mancini’s shortlist thanks to his recent rise to prominence, but the full-back was eventually snubbed. How Will Lazio Replace Zaccagni Against Napoli & Beyond? Three Options Emerge In addition to the usual suspects, the 31-man squad included fresh names like 17-year-old Como midfielder Riccardo Cassano and 18-year-old Parma forward Simone Lontani. However, the two teenagers are only expected to spend the first few days among the seniors before rejoining Italy’s U18 and U19 squads respectively. Italy Will Play France & Belgium The Azzurri will host France at San Siro on November 12 before playing Belgium away from home on November 15 in their last two UEFA Nations League group-stage fixtures. Mancini’s men collected seven points in their first four outings, having lost to Belgium on the opening matchday, beaten Turkiye home and away, and drawn with Zinedine Zidane’s side at the Stade de France. They need to finish either first or second in the group to book their place in the quarter-finals. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-USA TODAY Sports Brandon Aiyuk is a name that hasn’t been heard in quite a while, as the San Francisco 49ers’ 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft has been missing in action. Aiyuk has not played in an NFL game since Oct. 20, 2024, against the Kansas City Chiefs, when he tore the ACL, MCL, and meniscus in his right knee. Afterward, the wideout clashed with the 49ers organization and skipped required rehab sessions and check-ins with the team during that offseason. As a result, in July 2025, the Niners voided roughly $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk’s contract. In December, the team placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list after he stopped making appearances at team facilities. But news about the wide receiver’s well-being has surfaced, per Aiyuk’s newly acquired agent, as he appears ready to play again. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , Aiyuk has filed for reinstatement and is prepared to report to the team’s facility. Schefter received the news from Aiyuk’s new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who stated, “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field.” Aiyuk’s decision to file for reinstatement does not guarantee him a spot back on the team’s roster, but the Niners must decide what to do with his rights. The path back to San Francisco doesn’t seem likely, though, after head coach Kyle Shanahan shared his thoughts on the situation. In a video of Shanahan’s Wednesday press conference shared by Ari Meirov on X , Shanahan responded to questions about Aiyuk’s reinstatement. “I have no expectation; I’ve kind of moved on with that mentally and everything…nothing’s really changed for me,” Shanahan said. Another reporter asked whether the Niners will ask for a roster exemption or even try to trade Aiyuk, but Shanahan shut the idea down. “Those are no questions I’ve asked, so I don’t know, but I have zero questions about him,” Shanahan said. Aiyuk is expected to appear at the 49ers’ facilities on Friday, and “once he does, San Francisco can’t turn him away. The options are to keep him, cut him, or somehow find a trade.” The post 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan reacts to Brandon Aiyuk filing for reinstatement appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.description: Lampard appreciation at Everton, Glasner sparking Forest fire, Zubimendi and Kroupi in spotlight and Carrick v Emery Premier League top scorers Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, will again be absent for Everton after his recent disciplinary breach, although the manager, David Moyes, said: “We will be working again with Jack soon.” Andy Hunter Everton v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times GMT) Leeds v Tottenham, Saturday 12.30pm Continue reading...

Bye Weeks: PIT, TEN Week 9 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Joe Burrow . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses. You can check my work here. My biggest miss was my Ride of the Week, Zay Flowers. He scored zero points. I’ll repeat that – A bagel. A donut. Zero point zero. I obviously couldn’t foresee the quarterback injuries, but I’ll take the L. My Fade of the Week hit (Bryce Young, 11.4 fantasy points, QB18) and so did my Sleeper of the Week (Geno Smith, 19 fantasy points, QB13). *** Ride of the Week: Matthew Stafford (@WAS). Stafford is ranked outside the Top-10 QBs this week and I think that’s too low. The Commanders can score behind Jayden Daniels and they also give up points. This game’s Vegas total of 50.5 is the second highest on the board and I think it goes over. Washington is tough to run on, but generous in the passing game. They’re one of seven teams that has allowed at least 15 TD passes so far this season, and they’ve given up the third most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing QBs. Stafford is coming off his second worst fantasy output of the season and I think he’ll rebound. He came out of last week’s game with a sore elbow, so keep an eye on that. Fade of the Week: Zay Flowers (vs. JAC). Well, this is a first for me, as Flowers goes from Ride of the Week to Fade of the Week in just five days. UDFA rookie Joe Fagnano gets his first NFL start for the Ravens, on a short week and a bad ankle. If the Ravens get to ten points, I’ll be surprised. Their implied total is 15, which is the second lowest on the Board, and they haven’t topped 13 points in any of their last three games. Jacoby Brissett will help – in Week 10. Jacksonville’s defense must be licking its chops after it throttled another dead team last week. Flowers is a terrific receiver who was having a great season before last Sunday, but this QB situation is too much to overcome. He’s ranked inside the Top-20 at the position this week and I have him outside my Top-30. Sleeper of the Week: Drew Lock (vs. ARI) . The Cardinals are coming off that improbable comeback in Dallas, while Seattle will look to rebound after getting spanked by the Bears at home. This should be a get-right game for the Seahawks, and a potential let-down affair for the Cardinals (who had a let-down two weeks ago, after their big upset win over the Rams in Week 6). Seattle may struggle to run the ball against a defense that just stymied Javonte Williams. Arizona has allowed the most TD passes (18) and second most FPPG to opposing QBs. Lock is ranked as the QB29 this week, which is absurd. He’s behind Fagnano, Gardner Minshew II, and Shedeur Sanders? No. None of them have JSN to throw to. Obviously, he shouldn’t be started over a Top-12 option, but I like him as a QB2 this week. In his only start of the season in Week 2, he put up 21 fantasy points at…you guessed it…Arizona. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Lamar, Drake Maye, Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who should smash: Dak Prescott (@IND). The Colts have given up, or at least, they don’t have the ability to compete at the moment. Dak should have his way with this mediocre defense, which has allowed the tenth most FPPG to opposing QBs. Dallas can’t afford another stupid loss. Trevor Lawrence (@BAL). The Ravens have a decent defense that’s middle of the pack against opposing QBs, but there’s almost no scenario where they don’t lose this game by a lot. Their offense won’t be able to stay on the field, so Lawrence should have plenty of scoring chances. Patrick Mahomes (vs. NYJ). Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three TDs at Denver, to break a mini-cold streak and this week he gets a much softer defense, at home. Kenneth Walker might run wild, but I think Mahomes will get his too. The Jets have allowed 14 TD passes this season and have only one pick (ahem, that’s since the start of last season). Sleep

item.description: Baltimore Ravens kicker Tyler Loop. The Baltimore Ravens entered the season with Tyler Loop firmly in place as their kicker after he spent training camp as the only kicker on the roster. However, injuries and missed opportunities have forced the team to make another change at a position that has already caused problems this season. With Loop now on injured reserve, the team must turn to a familiar face who has been waiting for his chance. Here is what happened to the second-year kicker and why Jake Moody will handle the job next. What Tyler Loop’s Injury Means for the Ravens’ Kicking Job and Jake Moody Loop is dealing with a right groin injury. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Loop was ‘dealing with something small that kind of became a little bit more,’ but did not specify when the injury worsened. Baltimore has since placed him on injured reserve, which means he must miss at least four games. He could become eligible to return in Week 14 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Loop also struggled during the loss to Buffalo. He missed a 34-yard field goal off the left upright while the Ravens trailed 13-7. item.description: Jay Monahan steps down as commissioner of the PGA Tour on December 31. He recently sat down with Golfweek columnist Eamon Lynch at his home in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, to discuss the highs and lows of his decade on the job. Their conversation was for the premiere episode of Golf Channel’s new interview show, Eamon Lynch Has Questions . This is their conversation. What's your rush? Jay Monahan: Ten years is hardly a rush. First of all, those are two legends, Deane and Tim. I think the simple answer to the question is this was part of the plan. I negotiated a five-year contract that took me through the end of 2026. When we completed that, I had made the decision that that would be the end of my time at the PGA Tour. That would be 10 years. And I think in today's day and age, and what's required of leaders and what's required of stewards, I though that was the appropriate amount of time for me to be at the tour, and ultimately the right time to have a new leader come in. Now, in answering that question, when I felt that, I certainly didn't know what was coming. But I never wavered in that that was the right timeframe for me and my family. By the time you leave, you'll have spent 3,651 days in this job. Pretty fair to say that one of those days was analyzed and debated more than any other, which was of course June 6th, 2023, when you announced a surprising framework agreement with the Saudis. I want to go back to the night before. What was your mindset on the night of June 5th, knowing what was coming the next day? JM: I was excited. I was looking forward to letting our players, letting the world know that we had entered into a framework agreement. And again, the framework agreement was a framework for us to negotiate. item.title: Dianna Russini Hands NFL Insiders Cryptic Return Update Seven Months After Mike Vrabel Scandal
item.description: Dianna Russini was left with no choice but to resign from The Athletic following an internal investigation into her undisclosed relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel . The situation grew chaotic for both of them as steamy photos leaked one after another, forcing Vrabel into difficult conversations with his family after the scandal broke. While multiple outlets repeatedly reported that Russini would eventually return, she remained completely sidelined through the 2026 NFL Draft and the first half of the regular season. Now, after seven months away from the beat, she finally seems to be closing in on making a comeback. Dianna Russini teases return months after Mike Vrabel scandal Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reported Wednesday that the 43-year-old media figure is telling people around the league about her plans. Nov 10, 2019; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; ESPN radio sideine reporter Dianna Russini during the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Los Angeles Rams at Heinz Field. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,'” he wrote. But Florio remains unsure about her exact role or which network she will join. Given the reports, it seems like her return would land the week of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. 𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚: Diana Russini will be “returning to work” next week as an NFL insider and reporter. She has already started spreading the word to people in the league. (via @ProFootballTalk) https://t.co/SdR9QabU3s — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) November 4, 2026 The sudden news appears timed to coincide with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline week. While Florio remains unsure of her exact destination or role, Front Office Sports’ Michael McCarthy had previously confirmed before the season that the 43-year-old reporter was aggressively planning a comeback in the media. During the initial fallout, industry allies rushed to her corner. Former ESPN colleague Jon “Stugotz” Wiener publicly offered her a co-hosting spot on his Fox Sports Radio show, Stugotz and Company, asserting that he would not bail on a friend during a professional crisis. But she didn’t accept that offer. Now, there is a mixed feeling surrounding her return. Former colleagues like Mike Silver predicted late last summer that Russini would eventually find her way back to the football realm, but many believe the scandal deeply damaged her traditional credibility as a transactional breaking-news insider. If she does return, industry expectations suggest she will initially pivot toward a personality-driven role centered on long-form interviews before eventually scaling up to a much larger position like before. item.title: Maximize views! TKO reveals talks to expand beyond Paramount+, including UFC on HBO
item.description: POLAND - 2026/03/03: In this photo illustration, a HBO logo is seen displayed on a smartphone with Paramount logo on the background. (Photo Illustration by Omar Marques/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) “ UFC on HBO ” could soon become reality. Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) officially moved its entire United States broadcast package to Paramount+ at the beginning of 2026 . However, the promotion may eventually spread its programming across several additional networks—including HBO and TNT. TKO Group Holdings President and Chief Operating Officer Mark Shapiro revealed during Wednesday’s third-quarter financial call that discussions are already underway about expanding UFC’s reach across Skydance’s growing media empire. “We will be maximizing HBO, TNT, Paramount+ and CBS,” Shapiro said, explaining that the ultimate goal is to increase UFC’s audience, viewership and overall engagement. The new possibilities stem from Paramount’s recently completed acquisition of Warner Bros . Discovery. The massive transaction brought CBS, Paramount+, HBO, HBO Max, CNN, TNT Sports and several other major platforms under the same Skydance corporate umbrella. The company also intends to combine its two streaming services over time. That gives UFC considerably more places to showcase its product, although no specific events, distribution plans or launch dates have been announced. UFC’s seven-year, $7.7 billion deal still makes Paramount+ its primary home, with all numbered events and Fight Night cards available through the streaming service. Select marquee events can also be simulcast on CBS. The addition of HBO and TNT could create new opportunities for live cards, major-event simulcasts, documentaries and other supplemental programming. That is only a potential outcome at this stage, but Shapiro made it clear that TKO and Skydance are actively considering how to use every platform available to them. A UFC card on HBO would carry some historical significance. HBO was once synonymous with elite combat sports, broadcasting some of boxing’s biggest fights for 45 years before abandoning live boxing at the end of 2018 . Its final boxing broadcast took place on Dec. 8 of that year. Now, nearly a decade later, UFC could return live combat sports to the iconic premium network. For fans, the biggest unanswered question is whether additional distribution would make UFC events easier to find or scatter them across several different platforms. Paramount+ remains the promotion’s central home for now, but the days of UFC existing almost exclusively on one streaming service may already be numbered.

item.title: Siena men's basketball expects exhibition to help in home opener vs. Princeton
item.description: The Siena bench celebrates during exhibition game against Syracuse at MVP Arena in Albany on Oct. 18 (Stephen Weaver) LOUDONVILLE - The Siena men's basketball team will play a home opener that isn't one in many ways. The Saints take on Princeton at 1 p.m. Sunday in their first regular-season game at MVP Arena, which also hosted the Siena-Syracuse exhibition on Oct. 18. Siena graduate guard Brendan Coyle of Niskayuna said the 81-76 loss to the Orange in front of 8,604 fans should help in an official game against the Tigers. "I think when you get to play a game that doesn't necessarily count in the wins and loss column, when you get to do that at home in front of a large crowd, I think it gets a lot of the nerves of playing at the arena for the first time and get your first shots at the arena, out of the way," Coyle said. "Now for the home opener and the regular season, everybody will be good." The Saints (0-1) will try to be better than they were in the 80-75 loss at Bryant in Monday's regular-season opener. They'll walk into an arena that already has the 2026 NCAA Tournament banner hanging from the ceiling. They unfurled it and collected their Metro Conference championship rings on Oct. 18 in a pregame ceremony that included Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara and three Orange players who were all with Siena last year. With that celebration behind them, the Saints competed hard with Syracuse. The Saints trailed by a point in the final minute in new coach Nevada Smith's first game in the building. "I think anytime you can get experience playing in your home venue with a crowd, it can really help moving forward," Smith said. "That truly was the first time we shot in there with fans, so it was a good experience for our guys. I think they understand the routine now, which is big for us. Our guys like routine. They feel more comfortable with the routine. Having a game under our belt down there is going to be huge." (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona captain Raphinha signed a contract extension on Thursday that is designed to keep him at the club until 2030. The Brazilian was thrilled to lock down his future and spoke about a number of topics after the signing at a press conference. Here’s a round-up of what Raphinha had to say: Raphinha on Atletico Madrid “We play a sport where it’s 11 against 11, and each team is looking out for their own best interests. We were eliminated, but we won the last match. I think we have a positive record in the matches we’ve played there. We know our strength. When we’re focused and focused on our objective, we’re very strong. We have to respect Atlético Madrid a lot.” Raphinha on Lamine Yamal “We don’t see competition from the inside, it’s more from the outside than from us, I would be super happy if he could win 10 Ballon d’Or, he deserves it for everything he’s doing and for what he’s going to do.” Raphinha on being Barcelona’s No. 9 “The movements I make as a 9 I have always done, making the movement behind the back of the defenders, but before I was further away from the goal. It’s something natural to me, not something I had to learn playing in the position. I watch Gabriel Jesus, Lamine, Gordon, Adeyemi to learn more.” Raphinha on retiring at Barcelona “It’s a very proud feeling. Only we know what we’ve been through internally since we arrived at the club until now with Barça. I feel very proud of everything I’ve achieved at the club, both individually and collectively. And obviously, I hope to have more years here if possible. Obviously, if my legs allow me to continue playing at a high level, I would love to finish my career at the club.”

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: The international break is almost here: so wave goodbye to your players, and maybe your manager | Max Rushden
item.description: What used to be a time to reset is now a time to rehire, and Michael Carrick is not the only Premier League manager looking over his shoulder Perhaps the most telling moment of Manchester United’s comeback against Roma was at the final whistle. The camera focused on Michael Carrick, who shook the hand of Gian Piero Gasperini before looking around trying to remember what you’re meant to do after a victory. The camera then cut to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, clapping with two of the most ashen faces you could imagine – as if it was a minute’s applause in the 87th minute for a lifelong, octogenarian fan who died peacefully in his sleep earlier in the week (most probably not at a United game but you couldn’t rule it out). Of course, there are rules about smiling when you are involved with a failing football club. Players can’t be seen to be enjoying themselves in the week after a defeat, managers have to be earnest at almost all times, apart from when a journalist’s phone goes off at a press conference – a moment of sporting hilarity on a par with a pigeon landing on Centre Court. item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Lise Klaveness: ‘Certainly there are people that can challenge Infantino’
item.description: Norwegian federation president distances self from Fifa presidency but believes governing body can be reformed As the rain whips around Oslo’s government quarter, Lise Klaveness is shielding herself from the wind, trying to work out tactics. “Of course we cannot probably do everything alone, but we have a voice, we have the right to speak, we have the right to suggest, so let’s see,” she says. “We will at least try to be a spearhead.” The president of the Norwegian Football Federation wants to re-engage Fifa, and other governing bodies, on the topic of remedy. A slightly arcane aspect of human rights policy in normal times, the importance of remedy became very clear in the aftermath of the World Cup in Qatar, when the families of those injured or killed in the work that led up to the tournament were left without financial compensation after Fifa chose to direct a legacy fund elsewhere. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.description: The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Subscribe to get our editors’ pick of the Guardian’s award-winning sport coverage.
